Long ago, when faxes were in fashion, we sent a polite-insistent letter to our customers using this miracle technology. And the letter had this line "Gentlemen, we insistently ask you to send us the act!".
Literally a couple of minutes after receiving, a frightened customer calls us, asking what the matter is, maybe an unexpected inspection happened or something, yes, they missed the date, but not that much; and he's ready to confirm to anyone that it's their fault. We were somewhat shocked by such diligence, and for our part also asked what happened that the most ordinary reminder letter caused such a commotion. To which the customer bewilderedly answered:
- Well here, you write "Lord, we insistently ask you to send us the act".
A few days later they brought us the act along with a copy of the faxed letter. And yes, the fax printed the first word so that at first glance it could only be read as "Lord". After that we kept wanting to write like that in every letter: it's very effective.
